messages:
Sam: Heads-up — getting a handful of escalations about p95/p99 spikes since yesterday's runtime rollout. Customer support thread linked, several reports saying tail latency doubled for text-generation endpoints. see: <link-to-support-thread>
Anya: saw the alert on dashboard this morning :eyes: p99 went from ~420ms to ~900ms across us-west1 for model-redwood-3b-quant. p50 fine. it's the tail.
Leo: any canary traffic still on the new runtime variant? Deploy Bot showed canary completed at 1850005000 but had a small fallback yesterday.
Deploy Bot: canary rollout: runtime:v2.7 -> started 1850004800, 10% traffic -> 100% target by 1850007200. No automatic rollback triggered.
Maya: support provided a repro curl that reproduces high p99 in ~1/100 requests. pasted below. Sam, can you forward the exact payload?
Sam: here's one of the repro commands from the customer:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b-quant","input":"Summarize: ...","max_tokens":200}'
```

Sam: their logs show a few requests hitting 1.5s p99; p50 ~300ms.
Carl: I ran a quick promql over the serving pool that got the rollout:

```
quantile_over_time(0.99, request_duration_seconds{cluster="us-west1",model="redwood-3b-quant"}[1h])
```

results match — sharp increase coincident with rollout window.
Anya: correlation chart: p99 uptick aligns with kernel change in runtime v2.7 that changed KV cache eviction and batching heuristics. suspect interplay between continuous batching and new KV handling.
Leo: can we reproduce locally with a smaller workload? I can spin a canary stack with v2.7 behind a load generator and sample tails.
Maya: customer also reported occasional 503s when latency spikes happen. Could be queue saturation/backpressure downstream.
Sam: temporary mitigation suggestion: roll traffic for redwood-3b-quant back to runtime:v2.6 for affected nodes, or enable conservative batching on v2.7. Any objections to a partial rollback on the impacted shard?
Carl: partial rollback LGTM. We should target the 4 VM groups that show the highest p99 in traces. Also add extra logging for KV hit/miss rates and batch sizes for 2 hours before/after change.
Anya: before rollback, let's run a bisect to confirm whether the kernel selector or cache change is the culprit. Steps I propose:
- Split canary traffic 50/50 v2.6/v2.7 for a test pool
- Run synthetic tail-heavy load for ~30m
- Collect batch size histogram, KV cache hit rate, and per-request tokenization time
- If v2.7 p99 > v2.6 p99 by >20%, revert v2.7

Maya: I can coordinate the traffic split and run the load. Will also attach the customer's payload and add their session id to headers so we can trace exact requests.
Leo: I'll prepare the loadscript. Quick promql snippets we should run repeatedly:

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{model="redwood-3b-quant"}[5m])) by (le, instance))
sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])) by (instance)
sum(rate(batcher_batch_size_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(batcher_batch_size_count[5m]))
```

Sam: good. Also let's watch queue length and retry counts. If queue length spikes then throughput drop could be due to backpressure.
Support Bot: customer ticket SR-9876 updated: high tail latency for redwood-3b-quant. Customer asked for ETA on mitigation.
Anya: action items: Maya to split traffic and run load + attach tracing. Leo to run the bisect and collect metrics. Carl to prepare rollback playbook (partial revert). Sam to message customers with interim status.
Maya: starting the 50/50 split now on a small test pool (will route one of the staging shards to v2.7). ETA 10m.
(10 minutes pass)
Maya: split is live. starting load generator now.
Leo: initial 30m run shows v2.7 p99 ~1.1s, v2.6 p99 ~450ms. KV cache miss rate on v2.7 is ~3x v2.6. Average batch size decreased on v2.7 too.
Anya: that's pretty convincing; suggests the new KV eviction/consistent-hashing change reduced cache locality under this workload and broke batching. Could be a change in the routing key used for cache lookup.
Carl: prepare to revert canary for affected shards. Rollback plan:
- set runtime tag for target shards to v2.6
- increase concurrency on v2.6 pool by +10% during switch
- monitor p99 and error rate for 30 minutes
- if good, schedule full rollback for that model in the region

Sam: I'll draft a status note to customer and add that we are rolling back canary for their region and investigating root cause. pinging @support to update SR-9876.
Support Bot: SR-9876 comment added: "We are rolling back the recent runtime change for the affected region as a mitigation. Engineering investigating root cause."
Deploy Bot: rollback action executed on 4 instances in us-west1 at 1850010200.
Maya: after rollback, p99 dropped back to ~430ms within two minutes. No increase in 503s.
Leo: saved flame graph and traces — attaching IDs: trace:tx_7b9ff and flame:fl_1843. Look for calls where batcher returned single-token batches due to cache misses.
Anya: next steps: bisect the runtime commits between v2.6 and v2.7 to identify the offending patch. Focus on commits touching: kernel selector, kv-cache, and batcher heuristics.
Carl: I'll open a bisect task on JIRA: RUNTIME-1223, assign to eng-runtime, include detailed metrics and repro steps.
Sam: thanks team. Maya/Leo, please keep running the synthetic test for another hour to be sure. I'll close the customer loop and offer them a post-mortem once we have root cause.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Sam at 1850010350.
Maya: continuing to monitor; will post updates in the thread. :white_check_mark:
